page_title: Learning to Fly: Let's simulate evolution in Rust (pt 1)

summary.title: Learning to Fly: Let's simulate evolution in Rust (pt 1)
summary.one_liner: You learn the conceptual basics of feedforward neural networks and genetic algorithms, as the first part of a series on simulating bird evolution in Rust.
keywords: how do neural networks learn without labeled data
takeaways: A brain can be modeled as a function from sensory inputs to outputs, here eye readings to speed and rotation changes.
A feedforward neural network computes outputs layer by layer using weighted sums, biases and an activation function such as ReLU.
Backpropagation needs labeled examples, so the author uses a genetic algorithm to let birds learn without them.
A genetic algorithm evolves a population by evaluating fitness, then producing offspring through crossover and mutation of genomes.
The series plans to implement the network and genetic algorithm in Rust and compile the app to WebAssembly.
summary.summary: This is the first part of a multi-part series that builds an evolution simulation in which birds with neural-network brains learn to find food. It explains the design: a 2D world, birds with eyes that sense food distance, and brains mapping eye inputs to speed and rotation changes. It then walks through feedforward neural networks (neurons, weights, biases, ReLU, worked example) and genetic algorithms (population, individuals, genes, fitness, reproduction). The implementation in Rust and WebAssembly is promised for later parts.
